source: SecVulEval dev split (secvul-split-v1), sampled from datasets/independent_200.json and datasets/vulnerable_fixed_200_pairs.json
notes: Few-shot demonstrations taken only from the frozen dev split. Code, labels and rationales are frozen in splits/example_notes.json. They are disjoint from both test files; the runner re-checks isolation.

detection.rationale: base_name[base_len - 1] is read before the string is checked. When the caller passes an empty name, base_len is zero, the index underflows, and the function reads memory before the buffer.

The function only unwraps a V8 handle, checks whether it is already a string or symbol, and otherwise converts it through the V8 API. It performs no raw pointer arithmetic, fixed-size writes, or unchecked indexing.
The destination's mrb_io is freed before the source pointer is fetched. When a copy targets the same object, fptr_orig aliases the freed allocation and the following mrb_dup dereferences it.
The function maps an integer constant to a static string in a switch and returns a fixed literal for unknown values. It allocates nothing and writes to no buffer.

repair.explanation: The vulnerable version collects the directory listing into the standard APDU buffer; the fix enlarges the files array to the extended APDU buffer size so sc_list_files() cannot overflow the stack array.

The vulnerable version treats only a return value of -1 as a read failure. A short read leaves part of the program header uninitialized, so the fix requires the full header size before the data is parsed.
